A11y Scope Summary) — `~ decision/run-diagnostics-off-terminal`: the start's trust step reports its word in one `trust-record` line under `diagnostics/`, never as a refusal, exit code or hint. This is the closest precedent for a new step in `viola run`'s start. An automatic verify at the start, its RED result and its recorded failed attempt have to say where they report. Under this row and the zero-viola-bytes rows that place is never the terminal while the child holds it, so the founder's "tell the user" form at P3 has to fit this rule or amend it.

**2026-11-18-session-folder-trusted-by-viola** (8. Cognitive Accessibility, two entries) — `~ decision/time-bounds-never-on-human` and `~ decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver` added "the start's Claude config lock wait" and "viola's own start" to the bounds. A verify run before or beside the session is a new time bound. These rows list every bound and say whom it falls on, so the form chosen needs an edit to both rows, and no human key may be blocked or delayed by it.

**2026-11-18-browser-tools-prompt-modal** — `~ contract/viola-verify/step-line` became `[NN/NN] … pass|absent|fail`, with absent only on the browser-tools-prompt row (PROVISIONAL, delegate overseer). This is verify's step-line contract, which an automatic verify reuses. It decides whether those lines may print at all when `viola run` starts verify, given that a passed run writes zero bytes of its own to the terminal. A RED verify must "say which rows failed", and this is the line form that does it.

**2026-10-13-interrupted-verify-cleanup** — verify stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM: no step line or summary, then `unable: verify was stopped before it finished` and `hint: run viola verify again to stamp this CLI` last on stderr, exit 1. It is pinned by the stop table in `tests/cli_verify.rs` and adds no time bound. An automatic verify that is interrupted (for example the human stops `viola run`) meets this pair. Its hint names the manual verb, so the automatic form has to decide whether the pair and its exit still hold when `run` started verify.

**2026-10-20-t06-58-31-wrap** — the interrupted pair's wording became the founder's own (the provisional mark was superseded). Changing that pair or its hint for the automatic path is a copy change to text he ratified, not a planning form.

**2026-10-26-home-and-code-bearing-file-integrity** (strict-modes refusals as scope entities, their text, witnesses and pinned pairs) — `viola run`, a `viola revive` start and `viola verify` over a home that fails strict modes refuse before any log opens, with exit 1, the home-state pair and `hint:` last. `verify` prints no step line, and `update_stamps`'s own strict-modes refusal gives the same pair, pinned by `HOME_PAIR` / `INSTANCE_PAIR` (`tests/run_cli.rs`, `tests/cli_verify.rs`). An automatic verify writes stamps through `update_stamps` and its lock. The order of run's strict-modes check, verify's `refuse_home` and the stamp write, and which pair reaches the user, is a constraint this chunk inherits (`contract/start-refusal/home-strict-modes`, `decision/strict-modes-refusal-before-any-write`).

**2026-10-26-home-and-code-bearing-file-integrity** (an unstattable home, per OS) — a home under a regular file is a strict-modes refusal: verify gives the home-state pair with exit 1. This is the row `decision/unstattable-home-is-strict-modes-refusal`, which a verify started from `run` still has to honour.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** (strict-modes refusals, the Windows ACL and NotFound arms retired) — the unstattable-home oracle is now the home-state pair alone, and the strict-modes cases run on ubuntu-latest. This is the current shape of the verify and run refusal witnesses an automatic verify extends.

**2026-10-10-viola-revive** — a passed `viola revive` enters the same TUI passthrough as `viola run` and writes no line of its own while the child holds the terminal (`tests/chaos_revive.rs`). Its exit-1 refusals use the fixed-message `unable:` / `hint:` form, and the zero-SGR list names a passed revive. The scope extends the automatic stamp to revive's start where the version gate is shared, so every output of the automatic verify on that path is bound by these clauses.

**2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract** — `revive` takes `--json`: each exit-1 refusal is one `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` document with empty stderr. The human pair stays byte-identical. A verify run at revive's start that refuses or fails has to fit both forms.

**2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue** (`viola revive --json` documents every refusal of its start) — every refusal of the start revive shares with `run` prints one exit-1 document. A `pump_child` error prints none, because the child held the terminal, and viola writes nothing past it. This is the trap for a new refusal or outcome at the shared start: it needs a closed `error` code under `revive --json` (`contract/viola-revive-json/start-refusal`, `contract/start-json-refusal/document`), or it must stay a non-refusal like the trust step.

**2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue** (a start against a holder; the `cli` catch site's `internal-error` document) — this entry made `stale-heartbeat` and `already-live` exit 1's holder causes. Under `--json` a fault prints the `internal-error` document, while `run`, revive's start, `mcp` and `hook` stay silent there. It bounds how an automatic verify that faults at the start may surface (`contract/json-fault/internal-error`, `contract/start-holder-refusal/*`).

**2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue** (the exit-cause table and one hint per code; the `unwrapped-name` and `endpoint-lost` hints) — `no_two_codes_share_a_hint`, `no_hint_names_release` and the exit-cause table in `tests/cross_exit_causes.rs` hold each code to its own hint. New hints are pinned by `send_hint_is_the_design_string`. A new code or hint (for example a recorded failed attempt, or what clears it) has to join this table and stay distinct from verify's existing hint.

**2026-11-01-unix-endpoint-and-home-hardening** (a refused socket directory at the start) — the socket-directory refusal at `run` and revive's start comes before any snapshot, bind or child. It added revive's code `socket-dir-refused` (the founder's own word) and extended the fixed-message form to `viola run`. This is the precedent that a new start-time code is a closed-word widening needing the founder's word, and it fixes the existing order of start steps that an automatic verify has to slot into.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** (revive's start refusals without batch-script-child) — revive's `--json` exit-1 codes became ten, after a closed word left with its emitter by the overseer's technical answer. This is the current closed set (`contract/revive-json-refusal/*`) and how it has been narrowed or widened before.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** (the tui boundary on openpty alone) — the zero-viola-bytes case compares the outer-PTY stream byte for byte with an unwrapped fake-agent run, and each boundary clause is its own nextest case on ubuntu-latest. An automatic verify run before or beside the session must leave this comparison green, with no viola literal, `hint:` or SGR on the terminal (`decision/zero-viola-bytes-on-the-terminal`, `contract/tui-passthrough/viola-terminal-bytes`).

**2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through** — a start variant got its own zero-viola-bytes reading (`passthrough_with_a_statusline_source_adds_no_viola_bytes`), and its time bound was recorded with whom it falls on. This is the precedent for a new `viola run` start variant, here one that meets an unstamped version: it gets its own boundary reading and its bound recorded. The arm itself was later retired.

**2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board** — revive's start makes one bounded `claude agents --json` read (5 s kill) that fails open, and the bound falls on viola's own child. This is the precedent for a child viola spawns at the start (an automatic verify spawns `claude`). Its bound and its fail-open outcome have to be stated the same way, and the board's CLI cell (`unverified-cli`) is the board state this chunk changes.

**2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint** — a `viola send` on a verified CLI waits in the readiness gate (8.5 s). A human key during the wait takes the wheel and the send is refused `human-typing`. Once a session turns verified automatically (especially "beside the session", verified when the stamp lands), the gate and its human-wins rule apply to it. `contract/send-refusal/input-not-ready` and `decision/human-key-takes-the-wheel` bind that switch.

**2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row** — a `/compact` send on a verified CLI confirms within 40 s, otherwise within 10 s, else `no-prompt-submitted`. The confirm windows depend on verified state, so a session that turns verified partway through moves which window applies (`contract/send-refusal/no-prompt-submitted`).

**2026-10-19-dialog-hold-for-the-driver** — the dialog hold (`dialog_hold_s`, 60–3600, default 60) bounds the driver only, and any human key hands the dialog back. This is `contract/config-json/dialog-hold-s`, the existing model for a `config.json` key: read once at the wrapper's start, with an invalid value falling back and logging one `parse-rejected`. A consent key, if that is the founder's form, joins this closed key set.

**2026-11-06-version-done-check** (the dialog hold bounds owned by 0.2.0's first entry) — this entry records that an unverified CLI replies `null` to a dialog at once, so the hold was not read live. It is the a11y-visible effect of `unverified-cli` on the dialog critical path that an automatic stamp removes.

**2026-11-14-budget-gate-removed** (8. Cognitive Accessibility; 6. Visual Design Verification) — `config.json` lost `five_hour` / `seven_day`. Exit 11 was retired and never reused, and an older wrapper's `budget-paused` now reads `unknown` (14). `budget-paused` left `decision/state-carried-by-printed-word`. This is the precedent for changing the closed config set and the exit map, and it shows a retired exit is never reused, so a new outcome cannot take 11.

**2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list** — the board's caption NAME · LIVE · STATUS · WHEEL · DIALOG · CLI is pinned by literal, and each state is carried by its word. The CLI column's `unverified-cli` word is the board state an automatic stamp flips, held by `decision/critical-path-cli-board-output`.

**2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline** — this entry built the colour decision (`NO_COLOR`, `TERM`, `COLORTERM`, stdout's TTY state, with no SGR under `--json` or a passthrough role) and the rule that every SGR span sits beside its word. Any new automatic-verify line printed on a terminal (a notice, or a RED row list) falls under these rules, and `unable` / `fail` are never coloured.

**2026-11-06-version-done-check** (cli checks on `std::process::Command` with literal pins; the §8 verification lines pinned by literal) — every fixed CLI string, refusal layout, typed exit code and hint-free `--json` is pinned by literal over `std::process::Command` on ubuntu-latest. Any new fixed text this chunk adds (a consent notice, a RED summary, what clears a failed attempt) needs a literal pin (`decision/fixed-cli-strings-pinned`, `decision/refusal-layout-literal-pins`).

**2026-10-31-sanitised-error-surfaces** (`--json` one document and its exit-2 exception; the `--json` failure documents' witness) — each `--json` failure is one clean document with a literal exit, empty stderr and no ESC byte (`cli_error_documents_hold_no_path_or_upstream_text`). The only exception is the `answer` and `send` exit-2 paths. A new failure path from the automatic verify must hold this, with no path or upstream text (no version string from `claude`) in the body.

**2026-10-31-sanitised-error-surfaces** (a peer's refusal screened to a code word; `unknown`'s detail; the census of error writers) — a word outside the closed refusal list stays visible with exit 14. `unknown`'s detail is a code word or nothing, and it carries no hint. Each error body names a writer and a witness, and `thiserror` messages interpolate nothing (`tests/contract_error_bodies.rs`). A new error type or writer for the automatic verify has to be named in that census.

**2026-09-28-mutation-testing-to-the-epoch-boundary** — the CLI output-discipline invariants (P4, P6) are covered by the epoch-boundary `run --mutants` audit, not a per-chunk gate (`decision/mutation-audit-covers-crate-invariants`).

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** (the manual screen-reader pass, Orca on Linux alone; the a11y cases' CI home) — the manual pass is Orca (GNOME Terminal for the cli, foot on Hyprland for the tui), founder-owned and gating nothing. The cli and tui cases run in the `coverage` suite on ubuntu-latest alone. This is where this chunk's new output-discipline and boundary cases land (`decision/manual-orca-pass`, `decision/manual-a11y-pass-gates-nothing`).

**2026-11-01-t02-46-44-wrap** — the founder kept the a11y tier at `Standard (1)` (`decision/a11y-tier-standard`). This chunk works inside that tier, with output-discipline and boundary assertions only and no conformance claim.

**2026-11-06-version-done-check** (the outer-PTY driver on portable-pty =0.9.0) — the tui boundary driver is portable-pty `=0.9.0`, which a11y inherits and never re-pins (`decision/tui-boundary-driver-pin`, `decision/portable-pty-outer-pty-driver`).

**2026-10-27-bounded-inputs-at-every-boundary** — the passthrough boundary still holds after a contained vt100 feed panic: the driver's `send` is refused `input-not-ready` while a human key reaches the child, and no viola literal reaches the outer terminal. This is the picked row `contract/tui-passthrough/vt100-feed-panic`, which a verified-from-start session keeps.

**2026-10-04-the-wheel** — the closed non-editing list (focus, mouse, terminal replies), with every other byte taking the wheel. This is where `decision/send-refused-while-human-typing` and `decision/stdin-classifier-non-editing-list` came from. A verify run beside a live session must not type into or move the wheel of the human's session.

**2026-11-20-a-quoted-modal-never-blocks-a-send** — `~ decision/no-screen-content-parsing`: the TUI screen is parsed only for compiled signatures and the compiled shapes over them (PROVISIONAL). Verify's probes started automatically by the product stay inside this ban, not inside the test-only rig's exception (see the next record).

**2026-11-19-a-fired-scheduled-wake-keeps-the-wheel** — the latest `except` of `decision/no-screen-content-parsing`: the test-only rig reads closed words only (selector place, box state, modals, box-row cell attributes). The trap: those rig reads are test-only. An automatic verify in the product, or a scratch-home live start at this chunk, may not lean on them as product behaviour.

A viola run (and revive's start where it shares the version gate) that meets a claude CLI version with no verify stamp gets that version stamped automatically by verify, with no human running verify by hand, then goes on verified.
The driver's sends and answers are then no longer refused unverified-cli for that version.
A red automatic verify does not loop: it says which rows failed, leaves the session to the human as today, records the failed attempt so it is not repeated, and names what clears it.
The automatic form (before the session, beside it, a separate verb or flag, a config key) and what the user is told or asked before the first automatic verify are the founder's at P3.
Verify's own runs, probes, typed bytes and dialog answers stay as they are unless the founder's form needs it; proved over the fake agent, never the live home.

body: The unverified-cli state and its exit 12: after an automatic stamp lands the session turns verified and send and answer are no longer refused unverified-cli for that version; with no stamp they still are.

New fixed CLI copy the chunk adds (the notice or question before the first automatic verify, the line naming failed rows, the line naming what clears a recorded failed attempt) comes from design and is pinned by literal.
A red automatic verify's output: the verify step line form, failure and unable words never coloured, a word beside every SGR span, no SGR off a terminal, static linear output with no spinner.

Indirect, through viola run's TUI passthrough: an automatic verify run before or beside the session puts zero viola bytes on the child's terminal; its diagnostics never reach the terminal and go to the run diagnostics.

Indirect, through the wheel: while an automatic verify runs beside a session, human keystrokes are never blocked and a human key still takes the wheel; after a red verify the session is the human's as today.
Time bounds of the automatic verify fall on the driver only, never on the human; no harsh timeout without warning.

Any new refusal of run or revive start (a recorded failed attempt, a refused automatic verify): unable line with its kebab-case reason code beside a plain word, one hint per code, the hint ending the refusal and naming what clears it, never naming release; stderr layout as the refusal contract holds it.
Under --json, run and revive start keep one clean refusal or failure document with no hint; any new code word joins the document's code-word format.
An automatic verify interrupted keeps verify's interrupted pair and its exit 1 stderr lines.
Printed claude version strings and failed-row names from the CLI are printed with C0 and C1 control characters escaped.
New error bodies have a writer and a witness, read as word, detail and hint, carry no stack trace or bare status, and their thiserror messages interpolate nothing; faults carry no hint.
If the founder's form is a consent config key, it joins config.json's closed key set as a contract row beside dialog_hold_s.
Proof over the fake agent: any live start is a scratch viola home under the rig, and live readings never gate; manual screen-reader or keyboard passes stay supplemental and gate nothing.

viola plugin install output and its exit 21: the plugin install is not reached.
viola revive --list human rows and --json output: the listing of revivable sessions is unchanged.
MCP server frame tools, frame verb refusals and hook event and dialog call refusals (socket directory, strict modes, server verify): the channel and hook paths are not changed.
viola wait output, its waiting line and timed_out, and the MCP wait tool's timeout_ms: waiting is not reached.
viola list board visual rows: NAME bold and truncation, DIALOG amber, stale-row dim and caption order are unchanged.
instance-unreachable details and exit 21 under --json: reaching a running instance is not changed.
Absences of a web or graphical frontend, a touch surface, internationalization and a rendered page: nothing the chunk adds is one.
Screen-reader target and test setup rows (Orca with GNOME Terminal or foot): no screen-reader setup changes.

**2026-09-28-capability-ledger-and-viola-verify** (the landed ledger rows, `viola verify`'s probe, the stamps envelope) — created the closed ledger, `viola verify [--record] [-- <program>]`, the stamps envelope `{"v":1,"writer":"verify",…}` whose merge keeps unknown versions and fields, and its one writer `update_stamps`; a failing row still stamps and exits 1; `--version` is read bounded (5 s kill, first line `X.Y.Z (Claude Code)`). This is the whole machinery an automatic stamp must call or reuse, and the precedent that a red verify still writes a stamp, which bears on how a failed automatic attempt is recorded and not repeated.

**2026-09-28-capability-ledger-and-viola-verify** (the version gate placed and split by crate) — set the start order with `run::version_gate` (a `version-probe` pair, the stamps read, `cli_version` / `cli_verified` into the first snapshot, nothing printed) and split the gate three ways: parsing and verdict in the pure `viola-agent-claude`, the spawn in the root `run::version_gate`, stamps I/O in `viola_state::stamps`. Any automatic stamp hooks into this gate and must keep that split, since `viola-agent-claude` stays pure.

**2026-09-29-verify-stamped-test-homes-and-harness** (verify's spawn pairs, the harness CI read, verify-stamped homes) — harness homes are stamped by `viola verify` against the fake agent; stamps come only from `viola verify`; `run --local-live` refuses under CI (`live-in-ci`), and the real CLI never runs in CI. This is the constraint behind decision/no-live-claude-in-ci and decision/real-claude-local-only. An automatic verify started by `run` must not spawn the real CLI in CI, and its tests must stay on the fake agent.

**2026-10-04-dialog-answers-by-dialog-id** (the strict stamps read) — `run`'s gate reads `ledger/stamps.json` through `read_stamps_strict`; a strict-modes refusal gives `cli_verified:false` and one `parse-rejected{parser:"ledger-stamps", detail:"strict-modes-failed"}`. This is the origin of decision/version-gate-strict-stamps-read, and the read path an automatic stamp has to re-read after it lands.

**2026-10-05-real-cli-verify-probes** (screen signatures compiled, ten rows, verify's interactive runs) — `run` passes `Some(&SIGNATURES)` exactly when `cli_verified`, so the full gate runs on a verified version and the partial gate otherwise; verify gained the PTY Runs A and B. Each widening of verify's child set was ratified by the founder live. A session that turns verified after it starts changes which gate `run` runs, and the precedent is that any change to verify's runs is a founder-ratified widening.

**2026-10-05-real-cli-verify-probes** (registry rows for verify's interactive runs) — verify's transient children run the user's global hooks and status line and leave CLI transcripts, an accepted residual; its probe dirs are 0700 and removed on every exit path (Run B's `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>/`). An automatic verify carries these same residuals and cwd-relative dirs into the user's project folder with no human present, so its form at P3 must state them.

**2026-10-05-permission-end-to-end** — priced one new row as "its verify probe and a re-stamp of both versions (at least 8 live sessions)" and declined it on the live-session cap. This is a precedent for what one verify costs in live sessions, which bears on the scope's spend and consent question.

**2026-10-06-local-command-send-outcomes** (send consumes the local-command list) — the verified bit reaches `send` from the version gate's `cli_verified` through `SendSlot::new`, and the send path reads no `ledger/stamps.json`. This is a trap: a stamp that lands while a session runs does not reach that session's send slot unless the chunk re-reads the stamps or rebuilds the slot (the "beside the session" candidate form).

**2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint** — on a verified CLI the gate waits for the input box up to `GATE_MAX_WAIT` 8.5 s; on an unverified one it stays partial. Its trap: a case that reads a verified, literal-less screen through a clock that never advances waits forever. This bears on tests that flip a session to verified (decision/partial-gate-on-unverified-cli, decision/send-waits-out-paste-hint).

**2026-10-10-viola-revive** (the replay's first product reader, revive as the second way a wrapper starts) — a passing `viola revive` goes through the same start as `run`, the collision check running twice. Its program resolution and version gate never read the recorded directory (decision/revive-program-resolution). A gate-time automatic stamp therefore reaches revive's start too, as the scope's "where the version gate is shared" says.

**2026-10-13-interrupted-verify-cleanup** — verify's Ctrl-C / TERM stop (`cmd::verify::stop`) is installed by `viola verify` alone. A stopped run kills its child with no key, writes no stamp, exits 1 `unable: verify was stopped before it finished` with `process-exit … detail:"interrupted"`, and removes only what that run created. An automatic verify run in-process by `run` would meet a handler `run` never installs and a terminal `run` owns, so the stop behaviour must be re-decided for it.

**2026-10-13-paste-newline-ledger-row** — when a row is added, a stamp of the older ids reads unverified, and "every home stamped before this chunk reads `cli_verified:false` until its next `viola verify`". This is the same unverified state the scope wants handled automatically, now caused by a row change rather than a CLI move; an automatic form keyed on "no stamp for this version" misses a stamp of a shorter row set unless it keys on the relied-row verdict.

**2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows** (three statusline rows and the relied set) — introduced `LedgerRow::relied()`: a version is verified only when every relied row reads `pass` (it had been every landed row), and `[NN/MM]` counts the relied rows. This is the origin of decision/version-verified-all-relied-rows, the verdict an automatic stamp must reach.

**2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows** (the resume row, Run E) — "a verify is six `claude` starts", and Run E resumes Run B's session in a guarded `-resume/` dir. This measures the model turns an automatic verify spends, the scope's spend question.

**2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board** (the agents-join row and Run B's agents read) — added the `agents-join` row and verify's one `claude agents --json` read inside Run B. `list` and `revive` gate their agents read on no stamp (decision/agents-join-read-ungated). This shows which start-time reads do not depend on a stamp and so are unaffected by an automatic one.

**2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers** (MCP list builds the board and reads agents) — "a new process spawning `claude`" was recorded as a boundary widening and ratified by the founder's own answer. This is the precedent that `viola run` spawning `viola verify` (and so `claude`) is a widening the founder rules at P3.

**2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline** — the colour reads were ratified by the founder, with the standing precedent that "any further environment read … needs its own ratification". This applies if the automatic form's consent or opt-out takes an environment variable rather than a config key (decision/no-environment-configuration).

**2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract** (revive takes --json on both arms) — registered `schemas/config.v1.json` as the tolerant `config.json` schema of the `CONFIG_KEYS` set. Under decision/config-keys-match-schema, a consent key for automatic stamping must land in both `CONFIG_KEYS` and that schema.

**2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row** (Run B's sixth paste; Run B's transcript files) — added the 24th row (older stamps read unverified, so every home must re-verify) and recorded that a real-CLI verify leaves Run B three transcript files and C and D one each. These are the residuals an unattended verify leaves in the user's Claude projects dir (decision/verify-transcripts-accepted-residual).

**2026-10-19-dialog-hold-for-the-driver** — added the `config.json` key `dialog_hold_s` (bounded, a bad value falls back with one parse-rejected line), ratified by the founder as a boundary widening. This is the precedent and the pattern for a consent or on/off key for the automatic verify (decision/config-bad-value-falls-back).

**2026-10-19-overseer-switch-to-viola** (verify's print-mode probe leaves an empty CLI project dir) — 4 new `~/.claude/projects/` entries per verify, accepted by the founder into the residual class. This is another unattended residual an automatic verify leaves on every new version.

**2026-10-19-newer-claude-cli-rows** — on a newer CLI (2.1.302) `for agents` vanished 15 s after the start, so a two-screen row passed while `run`'s gate would refuse sends on a verified 2.1.302; the row was widened and the literal added. body: The run start's version gate: on an unstamped claude version it starts the automatic verify once and then reads the version verified; the run log line's cli_version and cli_verified fields, the version-probe line and the run.version_gate span attributes carry the outcome.
viola revive start shares the version gate and logs as run; the same automatic verify reaches its start where the gate is shared.

The stamp stays written only by verify: the automatic form must write through verify's stamp writer under the stamps lock, never a second writer in run; verify's stamp-write and home-tree refusals still apply to it.

The driver-side send and answer refusal unverified-cli, the dialog log line unverified-cli and the version rejections counted by detail: once the stamp lands for that version these no longer fire for it; an unreadable capability ledger still counts as unverified.

What viola run may spawn: the verify process and its child spawn subjects (version-probe, verify-probe, verify-pty-probe, agents-probe) join run's child and probe lifecycle lines; any new subject is a word added to the closed diag-line subject enum.

verify's own output when run by the automatic form: its stdout step and summary lines, its exit codes 0 and 1, its process-exit details (interrupted, strict-modes-failed), and its lines carrying no content; verify logs only inside an instance.

A red automatic verify: a recorded failed attempt for that version that stops a verify on every start, a statement of which rows failed, and a named clearing action; any new event, detail word or state for it is a closed code with no path or pid, a distinct detail code per cause.
No retry policies: the one automatic verify per new version is not a retry, and a failed attempt is never re-run on the next start; no retry-once and no sleep-based waits on the stamp landing.

viola run stays silent on the terminal apart from its start refusal pair: whatever the product tells the user of an automatic verify (consent, spend, red rows) goes through fixed stderr strings and the start-refusal output, never interpolated content.

config.json's closed known-key set and its v: if a consent or on/off key is the founder's form it is a new known key, with an unknown key still a parse-rejected config-json line; environment variables are never a configuration channel to turn the form on or off.

Capability ledger path and stamps never logged: the automatic form's lines name the version outcome as codes, never the ledger contents, the stamp file's path or the probes' typed bytes and dialog text.
The home strict-modes and home-tree checks run before the automatic verify writes a stamp, and a refused home writes no line, as for verify by hand.
Any new span on the automatic verify path is a manual span with a static name, skipping all arguments, carrying no endpoint, binary path or env values.
Proof over the fake agent only: CI verify runs against the fake agent and a real-CLI verify never runs in CI; a live start, if the founder allows one, uses a scratch viola home under the rig.

Exit causes the automatic form can end a start with (including exit 12 where the gate refuses) keep distinct detail codes on the run start process-exit line, with fixed messages and typed errors of fixed Display.

body: The unverified-cli gate and viola run's version gate: a version with no stamp now sets off an automatic verify, and the session turns verified only when a stamp for that version lands; until then the driver's sends and dialog answers stay refused unverified-cli, and the gate's stamps read stays behind the strict-modes check.

Only viola verify writes the stamps file: the automatic form must produce its stamp through verify's own stamp writer under the stamps lock, never by viola run or revive writing a stamp themselves, and the stamps are touched only after the strict-modes check.

What viola run may spawn: an automatic verify is a new child of run (or of a launcher verb), so it must be resolved to an absolute program, spawned directly without a shell, with inherited CLAUDE credentials and parent identity variables stripped as for every claude child, and never launched as root.

Verify's own floors carried into the automatic run: verify never answers a dialog and never types into one, reads the screen only against compiled literals and signatures, needs a pre-trusted folder, keeps its probe effects in its own directories removed by drop guards; any widening of these is said whole at P3.
Exit 12 and unverified-cli stay the outcome when the automatic verify is red or not yet landed: the human keeps the session as today, and the refusal never blocks the human's own typing.

The red-verify record: a new piece of state in the viola home that a failed attempt for a version leaves, so no start repeats it, with a named way to clear it; it is written owner-only, through the one shared replace helper, its reader tolerant and strict-modes checked before use.

Saying which rows failed: the message a red automatic verify gives names failed rows in closed code words, interpolates no upstream text, path, pid or identity value, and full detail goes only to diagnostics.

The config file's closed key set, if a consent or on-off key is the founder's form: a new key is a config.json contract entry with its bad-value handling and tolerant parse, and no config key, env var or flag may switch off the unverified-cli gate or any other control, only the automatic verify itself.
The driver-permission rows: dialog answers and sends from the driver need a verify stamp; an automatically written stamp grants exactly what a hand-run verify's stamp grants, no more.

The residual rows the automatic verify now spends with no human in the loop: verify's trusted runs, its /context and echo probe residuals and its real-CLI transcripts, accepted risks that a run now takes on its own once per new version.
Nothing of the operator's real Claude home is read and viola writes nothing under the Claude home or Claude's config; the automatic verify writes only in the viola home it runs for.

Live starts confined: proved over the fake agent; any live run is a scratch viola home under the rig, its kept stamp owner-only and seeded to its own home, its credentials copy transient; the real claude CLI only locally, never in CI.

The automatic verify's process and log lines: a new seam, env read or child start it adds needs its log entry, the process-start claude-child line keeps names only, and the never-log floor holds on stderr and in diagnostics.

viola verify's own refusals stay its own when started automatically: its home-tree strict-modes check first, its refusal codes (strict-modes-failed, program-not-found, version-unreadable, pinned-hash-mismatch, unclean-fixture) are what run reports when the automatic verify cannot start.

The two CI watches re-read at their next red only: the cli_wheel pause-then-release test and the rig rehearsal's box-empty-after-x-and-del test; no bound, retry rule, wait or assertion moves to get past them.
